__
 
• The given sentence is in **past continuous tense**, which describes actions that were in progress in the past.
 
• The structure of past continuous tense is given below:
 
 
• **Active voice sentence structure**: *"Sub + was/were + V1+ing + object."*
 
 
• **Example**: *I was watching the movie*.
 
 
 
• **Passive voice sentence structure**:* "Object of active voice (subjective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject of active voice (objective case)."*

• When we convert **active voice** to **passive voice**, three things need to be kept in mind:

 
 
• Change **object** into **subject**.
 
• Change **subject **into **object**.
 
• Always use the **third form of verb** in the passive voice.
 
• Use** 'by'** before the new object.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• *"Subject (objective case) + had been + past participle + by Object (subjective case*)" **(Passive voice)**
 
• *"Subject + had + past participle + Object"* **(Active voice)**
 
 
 
• **Example**:
 
 
• *The book had been read by her.* (Passive voice)
 
• *She had read the book.* (Active voice)
 
 
 
• **"Sarah"** will become the subject of the active sentence.
 
• The conjunction **"by"** will be removed.
 
• **"had been baked"** will be changed to **"had baked".**
 
• Following the above structure, we get the correct active voice: **"Sarah had baked the cake."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 2".**

question:

solution:
The** correct **answer is** option 2)**

**__Rule__: Change of tense __does not take place__ with change of Voice form.**

Therefore, the passive form of the given sentence should also be in **Present Continuous Tense.**

__Formula for sentence in Present Continuous tense **(Active form**)__-

Subject + is/am/are + (1st form of verb+ing) + Object

__Formula for sentence in Present Continuous tense **(Passive form)**-__

Subject + is/am/are + (1st form of verb+ing) + (3rd form of verb) + Object

[the patient + is + being + treated + by the doctor]

(Remember that the Subject in Active voice becomes the Object in Passive voice, and vice-versa.)

Following this formula, we know that **option 2) is the correct answer.**

subject: ENG
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The government is implementing new policies to reduce pollution in the city.

options.text: New policies are being implemented by the government to reduce pollution in the city.
The government implemented new policies to reduce pollution in the city.
The implementation of new policies to reduce pollution in the city is by the government.
The government will implement new policies to reduce pollution in the city.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option (1).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **Present Continuous Tense** and Active Voice.
 
• The rule for changing a Present Continuous Tense from Active voice to Passive voice:
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.​
 
• Structure:
 
 
• **Subject + am/is/are + (Verb+ing) + Object (Active Voice) **
 
• **Object + am/is/are + being+ V3 + by + Subject (Passive Voice)**
 
 
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and** "The government" **is the subject and **"new policies" **is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject **"The government"** of the passive voice becomes the object, and the object **"new policies" **becomes the subject.
 
• **"New policies" **is a plural subject. Hence it will take a plural verb **'are'.**
 
• The verb **"is implementing"** will change into **"are being implemented".**

Therefore, the correct passive voice is*** "New policies are being implemented by the government to reduce pollution in the city."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In voice change, **TENSE **will never change.
 
• Be careful of the number of the object. Change the verb as per the number of the object.*** ***

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Human life will be prolonged by a new drug called new-med.

options.text: A new drug called new-med was prolonging human life.
A new drug called new-med will prolong human life.
A new drug called new-med is prolonging human life.
A new drug called new-med had prolonged human life.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The type of the sentence is **declarative** and the tense of the given sentence is **future simple**.
 
• The **subject **of the given **passive **sentence is **"human life"** and the **object **is **"a new drug called new-med".**
 
• The format of passive voice for future simple tense is: **Subject + will be + V3 (past participle form of the verb) + by + Object.**
 
• The format of active voice for future simple tense is: **Subject (Objective case)+ will + V1 (base form of the verb) + object (Subjective case).**
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• "A new planet will be discovered by the scientists." (Passive Voice)
 
• "The scientist will discover a new planet." (Active Voice)
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is- “A new drug called new-med will prolong human life.”**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 ("A new drug called new-med was prolonging human life."**) uses the past continuous tense, which does not match the future intention of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3 ("A new drug called new-med is prolonging human life.") **is in the present continuous tense, which does not accurately represent the future action implied in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4 ("A new drug called new-med had prolonged human life.") **uses the past perfect tense, which is incorrect because the sentence is about a future event, not a completed action in the past.

subject: ENG
question:
**Select the correct active voice of the given sentence.**

A brave fight was put up by the cancer patient and she finally won the battle.

options.text: A brave fight had been put up by the cancer patient and she finally won the battle.
A brave fight was being put up by the cancer patient and she finally won the battle.
The cancer patient had put up a brave fight and she finally won the battle.
The cancer patient put up a brave fight and she finally won the battle.

solution:
The correct answer is: **The cancer patient put up a brave fight and she finally won the battle.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the passive form and in the Past Simple tense.
 
• The Past Simple in the passive voice has the following form: **Subject + was/were + past participle + by object__**
 
• The Past Simple in the active voice has the following form: **__Subject + past participle + object__**
 __
 
• Passive: *A large house was built by him.*
 
• Active: *He built a large house.*
 
 
 
• In the active voice of the Past Simple, we have to change the structure, so the subject in the passive voice becomes the object in the active voice.
 
• ​Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct Active Voice:__ *The cancer patient put up a brave fight and she finally won the battle.*

question:

The teacher started a new game to keep the class engaged.

options.text: A new game to keep the class engaged was being started by the teacher.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active form and in the simple past tense and we need to change it to the passive form.
 
• The simple past tense in the active voice has the following form: Subject + V2+ object + rest of the sentence__
 
• The simple past tense in the passive voice has the following form: __Object+ was/were + V3+ by + subject + rest of the sentence__
 __
 
• Active: *Rohit called his friends.*

• Change the subject into an object.

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• As per the given question, we must change it to Active Voice.

• Subject + V2 + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*

• **"The crowd" **is the subject of the sentence, so we can make it the doer of the action by placing it before the verb **"laughed".**

subject: ENG
question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

The audience loudly cheered the student leader’s speech.

options.text: The student leader’s speech was loudly cheered by the audience.
There was a loud cheer for the student.
They all cheered loudly the leader’s speech.
The student leader was loudly cheered by the audience.

solution:
The correct answer is: **'The student leader’s speech was loudly cheered by the audience'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct answer of the active to passive is: **'The student leader’s speech was loudly cheered by the audience'.**
 
• The given sentence is in **'Past Indefinite Tense'**. The structure of it is: **'Subject + v2 (Second form of the verb) + Object'.**
 
• While changing it active to passive,** 'the subject'** (**The audience**) will be '**Object'** and the '**Object'** (**T****he student leader’s speech**) will be the '**subject'** and '**verb'** will be placed according to '**the** **Subject'** **(If it is singular, singular verb will be used. If it is plural, plural verb will be used**).
 
• Here, the subject in the passive voice (**T****he student leader’s speech**) is **singular**, So, **singular verb** (**was**) is used. Then, '**Past Participle form of the verb'** (**cheered**) is used. Next, **'by**' is used according to the rule. Thereafter, **the object** (**the audience**) is used.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **'There was a loud cheer for the student' **is not the correct passive voice.
 
• **'They all cheered loudly the leader’s speech'** is not the correct passive voice.
 
• **'The student leader was loudly cheered by the audience'** is not the correct passive voice.

subject: ENG
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

I kicked the ball.

options.text: The ball is kicked by me.
The ball was kicked by you.
The ball had been kicked by me.
The ball was kicked by me.

solution:
The correct answer is '**The ball had been kicked by me.**'

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To convert a sentence from active to passive voice, we need to rearrange the sentence so that the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The original sentence "**I kicked the ball.**" is in the simple past tense.
 
• The correct passive structure for a sentence in the simple past tense is "**was/were + past participle of the main verb.**"
 
• The past participle of "**kick**" is "**kicked**," and since "**the ball**" is singular, we use "**was**."
 
• The sentence correctly transformed into passive voice that retains the original verb tense and meaning is "**The ball was kicked by me.**"

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 4**’.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 ("**The ball is kicked by me.**") incorrectly uses the simple present tense "is kicked" instead of the simple past tense.
 
• Option 2 ("**The ball was kicked by you.**") changes the doer of the action from "me" to "you," altering the original sentence's meaning.
 
• Option 3 ("**The ball had been kicked by me.**") uses the past perfect tense, which is not the same as the original simple past tense of the sentence.

• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the given question, we have to change it into Passive Voice.

• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)

• The preposition "by" is used to indicate the doer of the action in the passive voice.

 ​

question:

 __

question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.**

In Japan, thousands of people were killed in the tsunami last week.

options.text: The tsunami had killed thousands of people last week in Japan.
The tsunami has killed thousands of people last week in Japan.
The tsunami last week killed thousands of people in Japan.

solution:
The correct answer is: **The tsunami last week killed thousands of people in Japan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Passive Voice**: Subject (Thousands of people) + Helping Verb (were) + Past Participle of Main Verb (killed) + Prepositional Phrase (in Japan) + Temporal Phrase (last week).

 
 
• **Example**: *The cake was baked by Sarah yesterday.*
 
 
 
• In the **active voice**, the subject performs the action expressed by the verb.
 
• This structure typically results in more direct and clearer sentences, especially when the focus is on the action itself.
 
• **Active Voice**: Subject (The tsunami last week) + Verb (killed) + Object (thousands of people) + Prepositional Phrase (in Japan).
 
 
• **Example**: *Sarah baked the cake yesterday.*
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

subject: ENG
question:
**Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.**

Agnes composed a song for her father’s birthday.

options.text: A song was composed by Agnes for her father’s birthday.
A song would have been composed by Agnes for her father’s birthday.
A song was being composed by Agnes for her father’s birthday.
A song had been composed by Agnes for her father’s birthday.

solution:
The correct answer is **'A song was composed by Agnes for her father’s birthday.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice** and expresses an action done by the subject.
 
• The sentence is in the **simple past tense**, indicated by the verb** "composed"**.
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"Agnes"**, and the object of the sentence is **"a song"**.
 
• **Active Format: **
 
 
• **Subject + V2 (past form of the verb) + Object.**
 
 
 
• **Passive Format: **
 
 
• **Subject (Objective case) + was/were + V3 (past participle) + by + Object (Subjective case).**
 
 
 
• An example in short is: "The teacher praised the student" becomes "The student was praised by the teacher" when changed to passive voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is ***"A song was composed by Agnes for her father’s birthday."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When changing from active to passive voice (or vice versa):
 
 
• The tense of the sentence should not be changed.
 
• Only the structure is altered to shift focus between the doer and the receiver of the action.

The winner of the competition was announced by them.

They announced a winner in the competition.

solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 3'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In active voice, the subject of the sentence performs the action directly.
 
• In this case, the action is "announced." The subject performing the action is "they."
 
• Therefore, the sentence "They announced the winner of the competition" correctly portrays the action in active voice, where "they" are actively performing the action of announcing the winner.
 
• The tense does not change as it will remain the same that is simple past tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 3'**.

**Active voice:** ***They announced the winner of the competition. ***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's analyze the other options:

 
 
• **'They have announced the competition winner'. **This sentence is in active voice, but it refers to the **"competition winner" **instead of explicitly stating **"the winner of the competition." **While the meaning is similar, it's not an exact match to the original sentence.
 
• **'Announcement of the winner of the competition by them.' **This option is a noun phrase rather than a complete sentence in active voice. It lacks a main verb and doesn't express the action performed by "**them**."
 
• '**They announced a winner in the competition**.' This option is also in active voice, but it introduces the idea of **"a winner in the competition" **rather than specifically stating **"the winner of the competition"**, which is what the original sentence conveys. Therefore, it doesn't accurately represent the original sentence.

question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

Raju sells flowers in the market every Sunday.

options.text: Every Sunday, flowers are sold in the market by Raju.

Every Sunday, flowers were sold in the market by Raju.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in Active Voice. As per the question we have to change it into Passive Voice. 

 The structure of the given sentence as follows: 
 
 
• Subject + V1 + object. (Active Voice)
 
• Object + is/ am/ are + V3 + by + Subject. (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• *Example: *
 
 
• *Prashant understands her. (Active Voice)*
 
• *She is understood by Prashant. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• Here, in the given question the subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• 'sells' will be changed into 'are sold'. (Active to Passive)

subject: ENG
question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

I promise to furnish all the documents required for the assignment.

options.text: It is promised by me to furnish all the documents required for the assignment.
It has been promised by me to all the documents required for the assignment.
All the documents required for the assignment will be furnished by me as promised.
It was promised to furnish all the documents required for the assignment.

solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is in Active voice and is an assertive statement. This will be changed to passive voice.
 
• The verb here has two objects, direct and indirect object.
 
• While changing the voice form in a sentence-- the places of the subject and the object are interchanged. In the passive voice, the object word is preceded by the word--by.
 
• The subject of the active voice changes as the object of the passive voice. The object of the active voice changes as the subject of the passive voice.
 
• In the given active sentence **I **is the **subject** and **all the** **documents** in the **object.** When we change it to passive as mentioned above the active voice **subject **becomes the **object. **And the active voice **object **becomes the **subject**.
 
• Out of all given options, we get the correct sentence in passive voice '**It is promised by me to furnish all the documents required for the assignment**.' 
 
• Thus **option 1** is the correct answer.

Given below are the rules of tense conversion from Active to Passive Voice and vice verse:

 
 

 
 
**TENSE**

 
 
 
**SENTENCE IN ACTIVE VOICE**

 
 
 
**SENTENCE IN PASSIVE VOICE**

 
 
 

 
 
**SIMPLE PRESENT**

 
 
 
He **sells** flowers.

 
He** does not sell **books.

 
**Does **he **sell** flowers?

 
 
 
Flowers **are sold** by him.

 
Books **are not sold** by him.

 
**Are **flowers **sold **by him?

 
 
 

 
 
**PRESENT PROGRESSIVE**

 
 
 
He** is selling** flowers.

 
He** is not selling** books.

 
**Does** he **not sell** books?

 
 
 
Flowers **are being sold** by him.

 
Books **are not being sold** by him.

 
**Are** books **not sold** by him?

 
 
 

 
 
**PRESENT PERFECT**

 
 
 
He **has completed **the work.

 
He** has not completed** the work.

 
**Has **he **completed **the work?

 
 
 
The work **has been completed** by him.

 
The work **has not been completed** by him.

 
**Has **the work **been completed **by him?

 
 
 

 
 
**SIMPLE PAST**

 
 
 
He **completed **the work.

 
He **did not complete **the work.

 
 

 
**Did **he **complete **the work?

 
 
 
The work **was completed** by him.

 
The work **was not completed** by him.

 
**Was **the work **completed** by him?

 
 
 

 
 
**PAST PROGRESSIVE**

 
 
 
He **was reading **a book.

 
He **was not reading** a book.

 
**Was **he **reading** a book?

 
 
 
A book **was being read **by him.

 
A book **was being read** by him.

 
 

 
Was a book** being read **by him?

 
 
 

 
 
**PAST PERFECT**

 
 
 
He **had read** the book

 
He **had** **not read **the book.

 
**Had **he **read **the book?

 
 
 
The book** had been read** by him.

 
The book** had not been read** by him.

 
**Had **the book** been read **by him?

 
 
 

 
 
**SIMPLE FUTURE**

 
 
 
She** will write** a letter.

 
She **will not write** a letter.

 
 

 
**Will** she **write** the letter?

 
 
 
A letter **will be written** by her.

 
A letter **will not be written** by her.

 
**Will** the letter** be written** by her?

 
 
 

 
 
**FUTURE PERFECT**

 
 
 
He **will have written** a letter.

 
He **will not have written** a letter.

 
**Will **he **have written** a letter?

 
 
 
A letter **will have been written **by him.

 
A letter **will not have been written** by him.

 
**Will** a letter **have been written** by him?

subject: ENG
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Those kids always watch cartoon movies.

options.text: Cartoon movies are watched by those kids always.
Cartoon movies are watching by those kids always.
Cartoon movies were watched by those kids always.
Cartoon movies watched by those kids always.

solution:
The correct answer is** Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The type of the sentence is **declarative**, and the tense of the given sentence is **simple present**.
 
• The subject of the given sentence is **"Those kids"** and the object is **"cartoon movies."**
 
• The format of active voice for present simple tense is: **Subject + V1 (base form of the verb) + object.**
 
• The format of passive voice for present simple tense is: **Subject (Objective case) + are + V3 (past participle form of the verb) + by + Object (Subjective case).**
 
• **Example**: 
 
 
• "The gardener waters the plants daily." (Active Voice) 
 
• "The plants are watered by the gardener daily." (Passive Voice)
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is- *“Cartoon movies are watched by those kids always.”***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 ("Cartoon movies are watching by those kids always.")** uses an incorrect verb form; the passive voice requires the past participle form of the verb, not the gerund (-ing) form.
 
• **Option 3 ("Cartoon movies were watched by those kids always.") **shifts the sentence into the past tense, which does not accurately convey the present, ongoing action described in the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4 ("Cartoon movies watched by those kids always.")** lacks the auxiliary verb needed for constructing the passive voice correctly.

subject: ENG
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

She bakes the cake.

options.text: The cake has baked by her.
The cake is baked by her.
The cake had baked by her.

solution:
The correct answer is **'The cake is baked by her'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice construction involves rearranging the sentence so that the subject receives the action of the verb, rather than performing the action. 
 
• In this case, "**She bakes the cake**" is in active voice, with "**she**" being the subject performing the action of baking the cake.
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence, and the verb is changed to its past participle form (**usually with the auxiliary verb "to be"**).
 
• In this question **is + v3 **is used in passive voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 3'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because it uses the present perfect tense ("has baked") instead of the simple present tense ("bakes") and does not correctly form the passive voice.
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect because this option changes the meaning entirely and suggests that the cake will perform the action of baking "her," which is not the intended meaning of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4** is incorrect because this option uses the past perfect tense ("had baked") instead of the simple present tense ("bakes") and does not correctly form the passive voice.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

I await your response.
solution:
The correct answer is **"Your response is awaited."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence **“I await your response” **is in the active voice.
 
• In this sentence, **“I” **is the subject, **“await” **is the verb, and **“your response” **is the object.
 
• When we convert an active sentence into a passive one, **the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence**.
 
• The verb is changed to a form of **"be,” **followed by the past participle of the main verb.
 
• So, in the passive voice, **“your response” **becomes the subject, **“is” **is the form of **“be”, **and **“awaited” **is the past participle of **“await”. **
 
• Hence, the correct passive form of **“I await your response” **is **“Your response is awaited”.**

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 3". **

subject: ENG
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

It is said that this is the oldest temple in the region.

options.text: This is said to be the oldest temple in the region.
This is told to be the oldest temple.
This temple is said in the region to be.
This oldest temple is said to be in the region.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option (1).** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the Present Indefinite Tense.
 
• The rule for changing a Present Indefinite Tense from Passive voice to Active voice.
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the passive sentence becomes the subject of the active sentence.
 
• 'It' is the subject and "this is the oldest temple in the region." is the object.
 
• Here in this sentence the part **"It is said that this is" **will be changed into **"This is said to be"**. "**This**" is the subject.
 
• Use of the expression "to be": In the active voice, the verb "is" is used in combination with the infinitive "to be" to express the state or attribute of the subject.

Therefore, the correct answer is ***This is said to be the oldest temple in the region.*** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Remember, both of these sentences are in passive voice, it's just two different ways to express the information passively. Typical passive-to-active voice conversion changes the subject-object relationship: e.g., "The mouse (subject) was chased by the cat (object)" vs. "The cat (subject) chased the mouse (now the object)".

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

Mandeep has repaired the truck.

solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "Mandeep has repaired the truck." is in active voice.
 
• In passive voice, the object of the sentence (the truck) becomes the subject, and the verb takes on its past participle form (has been repaired).
 
• The original actor of the sentence (Mandeep) moves to the end of the sentence following a "by."
 
• Therefore, the correct conversion to passive voice would be, "The truck has been repaired by Mandeep."

Therefore, the correct answer is **"Option 3."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1: "The truck had been repaired by Mandeep." While this is in passive voice, it shifts the tense from present perfect to past perfect, implying a different time frame.
 
• Option 2: "The truck is been repaired by Mandeep." This option is grammatically incorrect; "is been" isn't a proper passive construction.
 
• Option 4: "The truck have been repaired by Mandeep." This is also grammatically incorrect; it should be "has been" for a singular subject ("the truck") not "have been."

subject: ENG
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Lemon tastes sour.

options.text: Lemon is sour when it is tasted.
Lemon has been sour when tasted.

solution:
The correct answer is: "**Lemon is sour when it is tasted.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in active voice, with "**Lemon**" as the subject and "**tastes**" as the verb.
 
• In the passive voice, the object of the active verb becomes the subject of the passive verb, and the active subject is either omitted or introduced with "by."
 
• To make the sentence passive, we need to say "Lemon is tasted" and add "by someone" or "by people" to indicate who is doing the tasting.
 
• However, the sentence doesn't really make sense in the passive voice, because we don't typically talk about lemons being tasted by someone else. It makes more sense to keep the sentence in the active voice.

Thus, **option 3** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**Lemon has been tasted sour**," is grammatically correct but doesn't make sense in this context. It suggests that someone tasted a lemon and found it to be sour, but that doesn't tell us anything about the lemon itself.
 
• "**Lemon is tasted sour**," is grammatically incorrect because it doesn't include a subject for the verb "is tasted."
 
• "**Lemon has been sour when tasted**," is grammatically correct but awkwardly phrased. It suggests that lemons are sometimes sour and sometimes not, depending on when they are tasted.
